gaps.wanted: Which end of the rear the fan trays number from. The chassis silkscreens a mark on the rail beside each bay, and at the source's real resolution it cannot be read: the rear elevation is embedded in the PDF at 1.83 px/mm, where a 2 mm numeral is 3.7 pixels. Upscaling the page render to 600 dpi makes the marks LOOK legible - a "7" appeared convincingly on the rail at the right-hand end - but the same detector run on the embedded image at native resolution shows there is nothing there to read, so it was discarded. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE FAMILY IS NOT CONSISTENT. edgecore/exp100-32x and edgecore/dcs240 both number their trays RIGHT to LEFT. The bays here carry rel-pos 1 to 7 LEFT to right because a view has to order them somehow, and NO numeral is silkscreened, because drawing one would assert what was not read. A photograph of the rear at 5 px/mm or better, or any figure that labels a tray, settles it in one look.

What the lamp on each fan tray means. Every one of the seven trays carries a round lens at its top left - a bright dome in a dark rim, about 3.4 mm across - and neither staged document mentions it. THE DC SUPPLY CARRIES ONE TOO, at the right of its lattice, 12 mm below its stowed bail where no part of the bail is; it was removed for a round on the AC sibling's reasoning and the reviewer caught it. THE AC SUPPLY CARRIES NONE: its matching ring sits exactly at the deployed bail's root and is the bail's end seen in perspective. The trays' lens sits where no bail is. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page lists the six chassis lamps and the RJ-45's pair and stops; the datasheet names port, management-port and system LEDs and no module lamp. The lamps are drawn because they are there, with the library's default off/on states. No green/amber legend is invented for them.

What distinguishes the four lamps of one port. The panel draws four round windows per port and the guide gives the PORT one legend - "QSFP-DD800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)" - which is a colour per SPEED, not a meaning per window. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 hit the identical conflict on the DCS510, where the guide goes one step further ("100G Breakout: 1-4 LEDs Green") and implies one lamp per breakout lane; nothing here says that. The four lamps carry the library's off/on default rather than a per-lamp vocabulary nobody published. A port-LED table, or one photograph of a lit port, settles it.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Between them the two staged documents draw two elevations, a LED enlargement, two FRU figures, the airflow figures and a power-connection page, and not one of them shows a third face. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 9 bays (rear 9); `physical-context` on port group qsfp-dd800 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: BOTH DIRECTIONS, AS SEPARATE SKUs, AND THE COLOUR RULE IS SHOWN RATHER THAN STATED. The ordering table lists ten AC part numbers per model - five cord regions x two airflows - plus a DC pair, and the FRU table pairs PSU-AC-2400W-F and FAN-1U-1x1P-F with front-to-back and the -B parts with back-to-front. THE GUIDE'S AIRFLOW REVERSAL FIGURES DRAW RED BAILS ON THE F2B BUILD AND BLUE ON THE B2F BUILD, on both the trays and the supplies. Unlike the DCS240's guide this one never writes the rule in words, so the colours here come from its figures and from the family convention. See roc-ops/Portrayal#277. THE TWO BUILDS ARE DERATED DIFFERENTLY: the datasheet gives front-to-back 0-40 C at 6000 ft and back-to-front 0-35 C, "subject to used optics".

gate-1.note: PASSES, AND THE HEIGHT DISAGREEMENT IS SETTLED BY THE DRAWING RATHER THAN BY PICKING A DOCUMENT. THE TWO SOURCES GIVE DIFFERENT HEIGHTS AND BOTH ARE INTERNALLY CONSISTENT. The quick start guide's Hardware Specifications table reads "438.4 x 589 x 44 mm (17.26 x 23.19 x 1.73 in.)" and the datasheet reads "43.84 x 58.9 x 4.3 cm (17.26 x 23.19 x 1.69 in.)". 44 mm is 1.732 in and 43.0 mm is 1.693 in, so neither is a conversion slip - the width and depth agree to the hundredth of an inch and only the height differs. THE REAR ELEVATION IS ISOTROPIC AT 44 AND NOT AT 43. Rendered from the PDF page at 600 dpi it reads 2221 x 223 px. Against 438.4 mm that is 5.0662 px/mm; against 44.0 mm the height gives 5.0682 - 0.04% apart. Against 43.0 it gives 5.1860, 2.4% out. A drawing that is square on one number and 2.4% out on the other has answered the question. 44.0 is used. THE FRONT ELEVATION IS NOT ISOTROPIC and is measured on its own x scale only. It reads 2215.5 px wide - 5.0536 px/mm - and about 226.5 px of ink tall, which at that scale is 44.8 mm. The extra 0.8 mm is the drop shadow under the chassis, which the lower row bands show widening the ink to 2274 px where the top bands hold 2215. The face is taken as the top edge plus 44.0 and the shadow discarded. THE INK BOUNDING BOX IS NOT THE FACE, again. THE TWO ELEVATIONS ARE DRAWN AT DIFFERENT SCALES on the same page - 5.0536 and 5.0662, 0.25% apart - so each face is measured on its own and neither carries the other's numbers.

power.note: 2400 W PER SUPPLY, STATED IN BOTH DOCUMENTS, WHICH IS UNUSUAL FOR THIS LINE. The datasheet's feature list reads "Hot-swappable, load-sharing, redundant 2400 W AC/DC PSUs" and its ordering table names PSU-AC-2400W-F/-B and PSU-DC-2400W-F/-B as FRUs. The EXP800 and EXP100 supplies in this library carry no output rating at all because their vendor pages publish none. DRAW IS STATED TWICE AND BOTH FIGURES ARE RECORDED: "Full loading 1600 W (100% traffic, 32 x 24 W optics)" and "1254 W (100% traffic, 32 x 12 W optics)". The higher is the max. INPUT, from the quick start guide's specifications table: "200-240 VAC, 50/60Hz, 15 A max. per PS" and "-48 - -60 VDC, 53 A max. per PS". There is no low-line AC rating anywhere, and the guide adds that a single supply powering a fully loaded system must be on 200-240 VAC. THE PER-PORT BUDGET IS 30 W and is the datasheet's, qualified by it: "for all 32 ports all with per-port maximum 30 W capability ... subject to total power distribution boundary and thermal considerations".

sources.note: A QUICK START GUIDE AND A DATASHEET, AND THEY DISAGREE ABOUT THE HEIGHT. Both are staged: ais800-32d-qsg (7 pages, bilingual) and ais800-32d-datasheet. The guide carries the Overview elevations, a System LEDs/Buttons enlargement, the FRU replacement figures, the Airflow Reversal figures and a Connect Power page that draws the DC supply's face; the datasheet carries the ordering tables, the part numbers and the power ratings. FIVE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE STAGED AND NONE OF THEM HELPS. All five are 960 x 700, which is 2.19 px/mm on a 438.4 mm face - less than half the elevation's resolution. They settle colour and nothing else.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 16 QSFP-DD pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-31/port-32).

the-drawings-are-upscales-and-that-was-c.note: THE 600 DPI RENDER IS AN INTERPOLATION OF A 1.83 px/mm RASTER, and this was found late rather than assumed early. The elevations are embedded in the PDF at 836 x 118 and 832 x 108 px, so rendering the page at 600 dpi upscales them 2.8x. THE EDGE MEASUREMENTS SURVIVE. Re-running the seam detector on the EMBEDDED rear image at its native 1.8294 px/mm puts the inner fan rails at 150.3/153.6, 195.1/198.4, 238.9/243.3 and 284.8/288.1 against the upscale's 149.82/153.18, 194.82/198.18, 239.83/243.19 and 284.64/288.19 - every one within 0.5 mm, half a native pixel - and the native pitch of 44.83 against the upscale's 45.005. Averaging a vertical edge over 200 rows genuinely buys sub-pixel localisation; the closing arithmetic on the rear is the second check. WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE IS LETTERING, and two things were dropped because of it. See the fan-bay-numerals gap. A legend that is 3.7 native pixels tall is not read, it is guessed.

the-management-cluster-is-shared-with-th.note: AND THAT WAS MEASURED ON BOTH, NOT ASSUMED. The same scan run on this device's front and on edgecore/ais800-32o's puts the two SFP28 apertures at 394.77-408.22 and 409.21-422.47 here against 394.75-408.12 and 409.30-422.67 there - 0.2 mm apart on a feature 13 mm wide, read off two separate drawings. The cluster is one CPU/BMC faceplate and both models carry it unchanged. WHAT IS IN IT. Two 25G SFP28 cages in one bezel legended `1 (up) 25G (up) 2`; a USB-C receptacle standing PORTRAIT to their right, legended SS with the USB trident; an RJ-45 management jack legended MGMT and an RJ-45 console legended CONSOLE beneath them, bezels 393.98-409.41 and 413.57-429.00 by y 20.78-33.64 against std/rj45@2's 15.8 x 13.2; and a recessed dark strip along the bottom carrying a round reset button legended RST and six lamps. THE USB IS A USB-C AND THE DATASHEET CALLS IT SOMETHING ELSE. Both documents' port lists say "1 x USB 3.0 storage port" with no connector type; the panel draws a tall rounded slot 3.8 x 8.8 mm with the SuperSpeed trident beside it, which is a Type-C on its side. USB 3.0 is the protocol and Type-C is the connector, so both are recorded and neither contradicts the other. std/usb-c@1 is placed `rotate: 90`. THE SFP28 LEGEND ALSO PRINTS A TRIANGLE BESIDE EACH NUMERAL - the panel reads `1 (up) 25G (up) 2` - and only the numerals and the 25G are drawn. On the 800G wall the matching triangle IS a lamp and is placed as one; here there is no window to anchor it to, so printing the glyph would assert a mark whose nature was not established. See the sfp28-and-port-lamp-positions gap.

the-optical-wall.note: SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS ON A UNIFORM PITCH, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. 2D template matching of one cage column across the front face finds all sixteen at 7.92, 32.25, 56.40, 80.73, 104.88, 129.02, 153.36, 177.50, 201.84, 226.18, 250.32, 274.46, 298.80, 323.14, 347.28 and 371.62, fitting a pitch of 24.2410 with an rms of 0.069 mm and a worst residual of 0.114. There is NO ganging and no gutter: the residuals alternate +-0.1 mm, which is the drawing's half-pixel and not a block structure. edgecore/ais800-32o's wall on the same page of its own guide fits a block model instead - four blocks of four on a 23.424 in-block pitch with a 3.09 mm gutter - so the two were fitted independently and the difference is real. Template matching found it; a single periodic fit would have averaged it away, which is the EXP100's autocorrelation lesson applied before the fact rather than after. EACH COLUMN IS ONE STACKED ASSEMBLY. The panel draws a single bezel per column holding the upper aperture, a bright honeycomb band and the lower aperture, with the pair numbered `N (up) (down) N+1` on one baseline beneath it. Odd ports are the upper row and even the lower - the guide's own enlargement prints `31 (up) (down) 32` at the right-hand end and the panel prints `1 (up) (down) 2` at the left. ROWS. A row profile through one column puts the upper aperture at y 6.73 to 15.43 and the lower at 24.73 to 33.44 - a row pitch of 18.00 to the millimetre, and two drawn openings of 8.70 and 8.71. std/qsfp-dd@1's registry aperture is 10.0 tall, so the drawn openings are 1.3 mm SHORT of it and the registry figure is used anyway, as the EXP100 records for the same reason: the registry owns the aperture and the device owns the pitch. Drawn widths are 18.3 against the registry's 19.0, the same consistent bias. THE INTER-ROW BAND IS DRAWN ON A BACKING RECT AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Panel pattern decor paints only its holes, so a slot field on a dark panel is invisible; this band is BRIGHT on the hardware - a perforated silver strip between the two cage rows, whose lower edge reads solid at y 22.79-24.18 in the elevation - so each column gets its own light rect beneath the pattern - SIXTEEN bands, not one strip, because the band belongs to the cage assembly and stops at the dark post between columns. The left, top and bottom vent fields get none, because those really are dark slots punched in the grey panel and the pattern alone is what they look like.

the-panel-is-mid-grey-and-that-is-why-th.note: THE CHASSIS COLOUR WAS CARRIED FROM ITS SIBLINGS AND IS WRONG. edgecore/exp100-32x, edgecore/exp800-16o and the rest of this line all carry '#3f4348', which nothing measured. Sampling the panel between features on the front elevation gives #626366, #737579 and #5d5d5e, and the vendor's own photograph ais800-32d-2-AIS800-32D-F.png gives row medians of #676767, #696363 and #776f6d. Two independent sources, one answer: a MID grey. IT MATTERS BECAUSE PANEL PATTERN DECOR PAINTS ONLY ITS HOLES. On a near-black panel a field of dark slots is invisible, which is exactly how the first render came out - four vent fields declared and none of them legible. On the measured grey they read as they do on the drawing. The fix is the colour, not a backing rect, because these really are dark holes punched in a grey panel. THE FIELDS THEMSELVES ARE MEASURED: a vertical slot column at x 1.98-3.17 by y 6.33-38.98; two horizontal bands across the port wall at y 0.40-1.58 and 3.56-5.54; and a three-row field along the bottom from y 39.37 to 43.93, whose cells start at x 10.77 on a 3.17 pitch. THERE IS NO VENT FIELD AT THE RIGHT-HAND END. The columns from x 431 to 435 read a flat 67-69 with no structure at all; the right margin is plain metal behind the lamp strip.

the-port-lamps-are-four-round-windows-in.note: FOUR PER PORT, EIGHT PER COLUMN, IN THE DARK POST TO THE LEFT OF EACH CAGE - and they were missed entirely on the first pass because the triangles had been taken for the lamps. THEIR ROWS ARE WELL MEASURED. In one post the dot centres read y 7.32, 10.39, 13.36 and 16.42 for the upper port and 23.25, 26.32, 29.48 and 32.45 for the lower - a 3.04 mm pitch on lamps about 1.4 mm across. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 is 1.8 x 11.4 with its four lamps on a 3.0 mm pitch, photo-measured on the DCS510 of this same vendor, and it drops onto those rows within 0.15 mm. It is seated rather than a new part cut. THEIR COLUMN IS LESS WELL MEASURED, at about 2.0 mm left of each aperture's left edge. A constrained fit at the known 24.241 port pitch scatters over roughly a millimetre because a 1.4 mm lamp is seven pixels here and the cage bezel's own bright edge sits beside it. The offset is used as measured and the scatter is the reason this is not tighter. WHAT THE FOUR MEAN IS NOT PUBLISHED. The guide gives ONE legend for the port - "QSFP-DD800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)" - and draws four windows. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 hit the same conflict on the DCS510 and reduced its states to the off/on default rather than invent a per-lamp vocabulary; that is inherited here. See the port-lamp-semantics gap.

the-rear-closes-arithmetically.note: SEVEN INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED SPANS SUMMING TO THE STATED WIDTH, which is the strongest check this rear has. 4.74 of chassis frame, 53.69 of PSU1, 4.73 of rail, 311.68 of fan block, 4.36 of rail, 53.70 of PSU2 and 5.50 of frame sum to 438.40. THE FAN PITCH TOOK FOUR INSTRUMENTS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM WAS RIGHT. Bay seams gave 45.05, the bails' edges 47.08, autocorrelation 45.05 and 48.80. The bails disagree because the FRU figure shows they are U-loops posed at a different angle in every bay - segmenting the salmon in the seven bays gives seven different vertical spans for seven identical parts. 2D TEMPLATE MATCHING OF THE HONEYCOMB SETTLED IT: six of the seven trays match at 60.60, 105.60, 150.81, 195.81, 285.82 and 331.02 (the seventh is under PSU2's bail), fitting 45.025 with an rms of 0.10. The tray frames read on two separate row bands then give 41.65 wide with a 3.36 mm rail, and 41.65 + 3.36 = 45.01. A POSED HANDLE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT; the part that repeats is. THE SUPPLIES ARE 53.7 AND BOTH WERE READ. PSU1 4.74-58.43 and PSU2 379.20-432.90 give 53.69 and 53.70. The first read of PSU1 gave 51.2 by taking an internal seam at 56.06 for its right frame; the symmetry and the closing sum identify which edge is which. THE MODULE HEIGHT IS MEASURED HERE, NOT BORROWED. Horizontal seams at y 1.38 and 42.04 bound both module types, giving 40.66 for the supplies and 40.6 for the trays. 40.6 is used for both. The rest of this library's Edgecore 1RU rears carry 40.0 as an estimate.

the-sfp28-cages-have-a-lamp-each.note: ONE ROUND WINDOW ABOVE EACH CAGE, and they were missed on the first pass too. The elevation puts bright blobs at x 399.92-401.30 and 414.16-415.75 by y 2.90-4.28 - centres 400.61 and 414.96, 14.35 mm apart against the cages' own 14.5 mm pitch - and the System LEDs enlargement resolves them as white domes in dark rims, the same as every other lamp on this face. The guide names them: "SFP28 LEDs: Green (link/activity)".

the-system-lamps.note: SIX RECTANGULAR LAMPS AND A ROUND BUTTON, ALL LEGENDED, WHICH IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THIS LINE USUALLY GIVES. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page enlarges the strip and names every one: "LOC: Flashing Green (switch locator). DIAG: Green (OK), Red (fault). ALRM: Red (fault). FAN: Green (OK), Red (fault). PSU1/PSU2: Green (OK), Red (fault)" and "RST: Reset button". THE POSITIONS ARE READ OFF THE ELEVATION AND THE SHAPE OFF THE ENLARGEMENT. A bright-run scan across the strip at y 39.0-40.2 finds seven runs: the button at 391.40-392.00 and the six lamps at 401.50-403.08, 407.04-408.62, 412.58-413.96, 418.32-419.50, 423.66-424.85 and 429.00-430.39. Their centres fit a 5.482 mm pitch. The enlargement resolves them as rounded rectangles about 2.4 times as wide as tall, each directly BELOW its legend - not the round dots this line's other 1RU switches use, and not a mixture of the two. THE LIBRARY'S NEAREST PART IS BIGGER THAN THE DRAWING. common/led-rect-sm@1 is 2.8 x 1.6 where the drawing reads 1.83 x 0.75, and common/reset-button@1 is 4.0 across where the button reads 2.5. Both are seated at the measured CENTRES rather than the measured sizes, because the library's indicator vocabulary is what a reader compares across devices. The 2.74 mm gap that remains between adjacent lamps is why the oversize is harmless here.

the-triangles-are-printed-and-the-lamps-.note: AND THE FIRST MODEL OF THIS DEVICE HAD IT BACKWARDS. The panel prints `N (up) (down) N+1` beneath every column, and the triangles were first placed as common/led-arrow@1 lamps, which is what edgecore/exp100-32x and edgecore/exp800-16o do with the same-looking marks. THE DRAWING SAYS THEY ARE INK. The triangles are solid white, the same white and the same crispness as the numerals beside them. Every lamp on this face reads differently - a bright dome inside a dark rim - which is exactly how the six system lamps, the two SFP28 lamps and the round port lamps all render. A light pipe and a silkscreen glyph do not look alike at 5 px/mm, and these look like the numerals. SO THE ARROWS ARE SILKSCREEN and there are thirty-two of them, one per port, saying which row its number belongs to. No other device in this library prints this glyph yet. THE NUMERALS WERE ALSO TOO SMALL. They measure about 2.3 mm of cap height against the 1.3 mm font first used; 2.8 is what puts them at the drawn size.
